The '''2020–21 New Zealand Football Championship''' season (currently known as the '''ISPS Handa Men's Premiership''' for sponsorship reasons) was the seventeenth and final season of the NZFC since its establishment in 2004. Eight teams compete in the competition with [[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]] and [[Team Wellington FC|Team Wellington]] representing the ISPS Handa Men's Premiership in the [[2021 OFC Champions League]] after Auckland City finished Premiers, with Team Wellington finishing regular season runners-up in the [[2019–20 New Zealand Football Championship|2019–20]] competition, after the remainder of the competition was cancelled mid-March due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/88417?newsfeedId=634683|title=Premiership concluded, Auckland City champions|publisher=New Zealand Football|date=18 March 2020|access-date=12 October 2020|archive-date=4 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200604224353/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/88417?newsfeedId=634683|url-status=dead}}</ref> The change from ten teams to eight teams was due to [[Tasman United]] and [[Southern United FC|Southern United]] joining [[Canterbury United Dragons|Canterbury United]] to form a united [[South Island]] team, playing under the Canterbury United name.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://oceaniafootballcenter.org/2020/07/29/tasman-and-southern-to-merge-with-canterbury-for-2020-21-new-zealands-national-league/|title=Tasman and Southern to merge with Canterbury for 2020/21 New Zealand's national league|publisher=Oceania Football Center|first=Rafael|last=Saltori|date=29 July 2020}}</ref> Auckland City won the league with a game in hand, taking top spot for their 12th [[New Zealand Football Championship#Champions and premiers|premiership]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rogerson equaliser confirms title, home playoff |url=http://www.aucklandcityfc.com/news/1329/12/Rogerson-equaliser-confirms-title-home-playoff/ |website=[[Auckland City FC|Auckland City]] |access-date=2 March 2021 |date=20 February 2021}}</ref>

===Fixtures and results===
The season was scheduled to be played on a home and away basis between 14 November 2020 and 28 February 2021, with the finals series being played in March 2021.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/96290|title=Fixtures confirmed for the 2020/2021 season of the ISPS Handa Men's Premiership|publisher=[[New Zealand Football]]|date=12 October 2020}}</ref> On 27 February 2021 it was announced that the game between Hawkes Bay United and Eastern Suburbs for Round 14 had been delayed because of a [[Timeline of the COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand (2021)#August 2021|COVID-19]] outbreak that resulted in the Auckland region moving to [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand#Alert level system|Level 3]] and the rest of the country changing to Level 2.<ref name="level3">{{cite web |title=Hawke's Bay United v Eastern Suburbs postponed |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/100598 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=2 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210302193955/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/100598 |archive-date=2 March 2021 |date=27 February 2021}}</ref> New Zealand Football announced that the game was to be rescheduled to be played as a midweek fixture sometime between 8&ndash;12 March but is dependent on the Alert Levels coming down.<ref name="reschedule">{{cite web |title=ISPS Handa Men's Premiership games rescheduled |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/100693 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=2 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301061008/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/100693 |archive-date=1 March 2021 |date=1 March 2021}}</ref> It was also announced that if the restrictions in Auckland remained, then the game would be cancelled and classed as a draw with both clubs sharing the points. If that was to happen, then the final top four teams for the semi-finals would be Auckland City, Team Wellington, Hamilton Wanderers and Waitakere United.<ref name="reschedule"/> This potentially could cause more issues, as two of the teams (Auckland City and Waitakere United) are based in the Auckland region so was also advised that in the event that the restrictions where still in place when the semi-finals where due to be played, then the competition would proceed to a straight final to be played between the two clubs that where top of the league at the end of the season.<ref name="reschedule"/> This would then see Auckland City and Team Wellington play the final, scheduled to be played on 21 March.<ref name="reschedule"/> With the restrictions in Auckland being lowered, the game was rescheduled and played on Wednesday 10 March 2021. The result of the game decided on who finished fourth and faced Auckland City for the second Semi-final.<ref>{{cite web |title=Date set for rescheduled Hawke's Bay United v Eastern Suburbs game |url=https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/100835 |website=[[New Zealand Football]] |access-date=9 March 2021 |archive-date=9 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210309191043/https://www.nzfootball.co.nz/newsarticle/100835 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
